Loans Performance · Proposal for Investment team feedback

From the Loan Dashboard spreadsheet to Loans Performance

Today the loan book is kept in a Google Sheet called “Data for Loan Dashboard V2”. This page proposes moving that work into EP Central, under Reports → Loans Performance: the same columns, the same calculations, a Create button so the team can add loans and payments themselves, and formulas that work like the ones in the sheet. Everything marked Proposed is a mockup for feedback; nothing here is built yet.

Section 1

How the spreadsheet works today

The workbook has five tabs. Two are typed by hand, three are calculated from them.

TabRowsWhat it holds
DATA for DASHBOARD120 loansOne row per loan: company, UID, loan number, type (CGA 83 · RBF 18 · TRL 17 · LOC 2), size, start date, term, upfront interest, rev share, balance, repaid to date, maturity, accrued interest, monthly interest, pre-paid interest, minimal monthly payment.
ECF1678 paymentsEvery payment for fund ECF1, pulled in with IMPORTRANGE from the fund’s “Actual Payments” sheet.
ECF2169 paymentsThe same for fund ECF2, from a second workbook. Columns are in a different order from ECF1.
Historical Principal Payments1 row per loan × 1 column per monthEach cell adds up the principal paid by that loan in that month (SUMIFS over ECF1 + ECF2, matched on UID). Nov 2021 to today.
Historical Interest Paymentssame shapeThe same grid for interest.

The calculations the team relies on

ColumnFormula in the sheetIn plain words
Principal Repaid to DateSUMIF(Historical Principal, company name, total)All principal paid so far
Interest Repaid to DateSUMIF(Historical Interest, company name, total) + pre-paid upfrontAll interest paid so far, including what was taken upfront
Principal Balance OutstandingLoan Size − Principal RepaidWhat is still owed

Section 2

What goes wrong with it

Taken from the workbook itself, not guesses.

ProblemWhat we found
Status lives in the company name28 loans have “(Paid)” in the name, 19 start with “-”, 4 say “DO NOT SEND”, others say “Rolled over”. There is no Status column, so nothing can be filtered or counted reliably.
Totals are matched on the company namePrincipal and interest repaid are looked up by company name, not by loan. Five names appear more than once, so two loans of the same company can pick up each other’s totals.
Payments that match no loan36 payment rows have no UID or show #N/A (29 in ECF1, 7 in ECF2). They silently drop out of the monthly grids and the totals.
Same column, filled in different waysBalance is a formula on 4 rows and a typed number on 115. Maturity is a formula on 21 rows and typed on 99. Loan size is sometimes a sum typed in the cell (500000+160000) to record a roll-over.
Two funds, two layoutsECF1 and ECF2 keep the same information in a different column order; facility type is “TL” in payments but “TRL” in the loan list.
Test rows mixed with real loans11 rows are test or demo companies and have to be ignored by eye.
One month = one new columnEvery month someone adds a column to both history tabs and copies a long SUMIFS down 1,000 rows.
Not connected to EP CentralThe loan list in EP Central and the sheet are kept in step by hand.
Section 3

The idea in one page

Two things are typed in. Everything else is calculated.

  • Loans and payments are the only inputs. Repaid to date, balance, maturity, the monthly grids and fund totals are calculated from them.
  • A Create button on Reports → Loans Performance lets the Investment team add a loan, record a payment, or add their own column, without asking engineering.
  • Formulas stay. Calculated columns use the same kind of formula as the sheet (SUM, SUMIFS, IF, EOMONTH …), written with column names instead of cell letters.
  • A payment is attached to a loan by picking the loan, so there is no name or UID matching to break.
  • Status, fund and type are real fields, so “Paid”, “Rolled over”, “Test” and “ECF2” become filters.
  • One record, two places. The same loan shows in the portfolio report and on the company page, and can be created or updated from either.

Section 7

Columns and formulas

This keeps the flexibility of a spreadsheet: every column is either an Input (typed) or a Formula (calculated), and the team can add both kinds.

Formula supportProposal
FunctionsSUM, SUMIFS, IF, MIN, MAX, ROUND, EOMONTH, EDATE, MONTHS, TODAY and + − × /. More on request.
What a formula can readAny column of the same loan, and that loan’s payments (for example SUM(payments.principal)).
Overriding a calculated valueAllowed per loan with a reason, shown with a marker, so a special case does not need a typed-over formula.
SafetyChecked before saving, previewed on a real loan, every formula change logged with who and when.

Section 10

Moving the existing data

A one-time import with a check against the sheet before it is retired.

  • One-time import of the five tabs (Create → Import from spreadsheet), with a preview before anything is saved.
  • Payments are attached to loans by UID. The 36 payments without a usable UID are listed for the team to assign by hand.
  • Status is set from the name markers and the markers are removed from the names.
  • “TL” and “TRL” become one type. Roll-over sums such as 500000+160000 are kept as the loan size, with the parts noted.
  • After import, totals per loan are compared with the sheet and any difference is shown.
Keep the sheet during the change-over. Export CSV gives the same columns as the sheet, so existing downstream reports keep working until the team is comfortable.

Section 12

Questions for the Investment team

Each answer unblocks part of the build.

InvestingAccrued interest: what is the rule you apply by hand today?If it can be written down, it becomes a formula.
InvestingRoll-overs.Should a rolled-over loan stay one loan with a bigger size (as today), or become a new loan linked to the old one?
InvestingWho may create loans, record payments and edit formulas?Proposal: Investment managers and admins for formulas; all Investment staff for loans and payments.
InvestingWhere are payments entered first?Still in the fund “Actual Payments” sheets, or directly in EP Central from day one? If the sheets stay for a while we can import from them on a schedule.
InvestingTranches.Is a tranche a separate draw with its own start date and term, or only a label on payments?
InvestingWhich status list do you want?Proposal: Active · Overdue · Paid · Rolled over · Written off · Test.
InvestingCSV layout.Is anything in the sheet used by investors or finance that must keep its exact layout in the export?
InvestingWhat else should live here?Yield, IRR, fund-level summaries or other calculations you keep elsewhere.
